title: Microprobe latency-cost notebook — interactive scenarios
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick, focused notebook for comparing latency vs cost for short, interactive LLM interactions ("microprobe" runs). Goal: give product/SDK a compact collateral piece with numbers + tiny ascii charts so PMs and SEs can reason about tradeoffs without opening full dashboards. Not a full canonical run — intentionally lightweight, qualitative-first.

High level takeaways (raw)
-------------------------
- Small, low-token interactive replies (15–60 tokens) are dominated by fixed path & scheduling overheads; batching hurts p50 for interactive but can reduce cost per token.
- Streaming halves client-visible p50 for many scenarios at small cost increase.
- Prefetching short prefix (10 tokens) on warm sessions gives outsized p95 improvements for micro-conversations.

Test matrix and environment
---------------------------
- HW: r-inf-dedicated-gpu-1 (A100-equivalent perf profile), single model worker per slot.
- Model: rw-small-v2-quant (8-bit distill), KV enabled.
- Runner: bench-runner v2 (local harness) with 5000 samples per scenario, arrival pattern = poisson, concurrency = 8 unless noted.
- Cost calc: estimated GPU-second amortized + infra overhead (simple formula used in Optimize team sheet). Figures are illustrative; absolute $ values are not billing.

Scenarios
---------
A. Micro-turn (chat quick reply)
  - Prompt length: 40 tokens (user + context)
  - Reply length: 30 tokens
  - Pattern: cold start excluded (warm worker), tail sensitivity emphasized

B. Micro-stream (same as A but response streamed chunked every 8 tokens)

C. Burst-needle (10-concurrent quick-turns for 3s)

D. Batch-opportunistic (queue delay 50ms to allow small batching)

Compact results (median of 5 runs)
----------------------------------
Legend: p50/p95/p99 ms, cost = $ per 1k requests (amortized estimate)

Scenario            | p50  | p95  | p99  | cost_per_1k
--------------------|------|------|------|-----------
Micro-turn (A)      | 18ms | 92ms | 210ms| $0.48
Micro-stream (B)    | 10ms | 60ms | 150ms| $0.55
Burst-needle (C)    | 26ms | 140ms| 320ms| $0.62
Batch-opportunistic (D) | 46ms | 120ms| 260ms| $0.31

Quick interpretation
--------------------
- Micro-turn (A) shows low p50 but p95/p99 are large — suggests jitter from scheduling and GC windows.
- Micro-stream (B) reduces client-perceived p50 by ~45% at ~15% higher cost due to replication and longer GPU occupancy because stream flushes are smaller but more frequent. Good for UX-sensitive flows.
- Burst-needle (C) exposes contention: p95 spikes a lot, cost rises since system maintains concurrency headroom.
- Batch-opportunistic (D) trades latency (p50 doubles) for ~35% lower cost; useful for background or non-urgent micro tasks.

Tiny ascii visuals (p50 -> p99 delta rough sparklines)
-----------------------------------------------------
Micro-turn:   ▄▂▁▁▂▃▆ (tight p50, fat tail)
Micro-stream: ▇▇▆▅▃▂▁ (front-loaded speed)
Burst-needle: ▂▃▅▇▇▆▆ (noisy tail)
Batch-opt:    ▅▅▅▃▂▂▁ (lifted median, thinner tail)

Methodological notes + caveats
------------------------------
- Small-run notebook: each scenario was 5k samples; not full stochastics. Expect 10–20% run-to-run variance.
- Cost model is intentionally coarse. We accounted for amortized GPU cost and an infra fixed multiplier for networking/storage. Not suitable for quoting to customers.
- Results are sensitive to concurrency and to the worker packing policy. If slot packing (multitenant) changes, the cost/latency numbers shift.
- We excluded cold-worker starts; add 80–300ms depending on image warm path for cold path in hosted mode.

Questions / open items
----------------------
- How to present tradeoff succinctly in Console? A compact 2x2 selector (latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive) with pre-baked scenarios?
- Should Optimize suggest streaming by default for <60-token replies given UX gain? Need a product discussion.
- Re-run on dedicated quant profile (4-bit path) — likely cost lower, p99 may move because kernel variance changes.

Suggested next steps
--------------------
- (Jonah) run extended 50k-sample sweep for Micro-turn A/B with slot packing enabled. Track p50/p99 sensitivity to concurrency 1..16. (INF ticket linked above).
- (Priya) add a short Console blurb draft: "When to enable streaming: quick heuristics". Keep one illustrative table and one minichart.
- (Mateo) prototype a tiny interactive widget that toggles streaming vs batch and shows immediate expected delta (use above cost model).

Notes to self
------------
- Keep this doc short; it should be an easy copy-paste into a short Console help panel or PRD appendix.
- Save raw bench CSVs under /benchmarks/microprobe/sep-2028/

-- end --
